messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert triggered for private-vpc-ACME-prod: sustained GPU queue growth > 2m and autoscaler errors. Severity: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC-4321 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: 2078001233 - alert: private-vpc-ACME-prod.gpu-queue.length > 500 && autoscaler.error_rate > 5%
Maya (sre-oncall): on it. paging Raj and Diego. paging @Priya for runtime help.
Raj Patel: acknowledged, joining. any customer impact visible on frontend?
CustomerOps - Karen (ACME): customers are seeing timeouts on inference endpoints, error rate up ~28% since 09:34 UTC. They reported queued requests and 502s intermittently.
Maya (sre-oncall): quick status: autoscaler is launching nodes but many stay in PROVISIONING for >10m. kube nodes not joining. autoscaler logs show repeated provider 429 / rate limit errors.
Diego Ramos: grabbing autoscaler logs now. paste: ```2026-05-04T09:36:12Z autoscaler ERROR: provision failed: api rate limited: RetryAfter=60s
2026-05-04T09:37:05Z autoscaler WARN: reached max_unready_nodes=6, backing off
```
Priya Singh: runtime note: this cluster uses on-prem vSphere via customer's private API proxy. We've seen throttling there before during heavy boot storms. can we throttle boot concurrency?
Maya (sre-oncall): good call. current cluster autoscaler config: maxNodes=40, maxSurge=8, provisionConcurrency=12. provider returning 429s, so concurrency likely too high.
Raj Patel: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce provisionConcurrency to 3, 2) increase autoscaler backoff, 3) temporarily route non-critical traffic to hosted fallback (if acceptable to customer).
CustomerOps - Karen (ACME): hosted fallback would require security approval; customer's policy blocks cross-tenant routing for prod. not an option without legal signoff.
Diego Ramos: executing plan A. lowering provision concurrency on scaler. kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: autoscaling.redwood/v1
kind: ClusterAutoscalerConfig
metadata:
  name: acme-prod-config
spec:
  provisionConcurrency: 3
  maxUnreadyNodes: 10
EOF
Diego Ramos: patched. waiting to observe behavior.
Maya (sre-oncall): also reducing node bootstrap parallel jobs on our side (prewarm images disabled to reduce API calls).
Priya Singh: adjusting runtime to allow degraded mode: reduce batch sizes and disable aggressive KV prefetch to lower immediate queue pressure. pushing config to routing: `--batch-size=1 --kv-prefetch=false`
Raj Patel: can we evict low-priority jobs to free GPUs for live traffic?
Maya (sre-oncall): yes. running eviction for non-prod taint: `kubectl get pods -l redwood/priority=low -n acme | xargs kubectl delete pod -n acme --grace-period=0 --force`
Diego Ramos: note: provider API still returning 429s, nodes that started show `ProviderNotReady` in `kubectl describe node`. logs: ```Failed to register: timeout waiting for provider API```
CustomerOps - Karen (ACME): we pushed a ticket to our infra team to raise API rate limit and to check their proxy. they responded ETA ~30m.
Maya (sre-oncall): good. short-term: throttled provisioning + lower concurrency + evict low-priority should stabilize queue. next: if queue remains high after 10m, we need manual pre-provisioning (create 4 warmed nodes via partner phone).
Raj Patel: I'm going to take the customer-side escalation for quota bump. Diego continue watching autoscaler events and node join logs; Priya watch inference latency and error rates.
Diego Ramos: watching: `kubectl get events -n kube-system --sort-by='.metadata.creationTimestamp' | tail -n 30` shows repeated `provider rate limited` entries.
Priya Singh: telemetry: p99 latency peaked at 4.8s, error rate 30% -> trending down slightly after evictions. embedding pipeline backpressure detected at router level.
Maya (sre-oncall): setting incident channel mode: page-only for oncall. tagging this thread with #paging #gpu #vpc-autoscale.
IncidentBot: Incident assigned to Maya (sre-oncall). Runbook: GPU-EXHAUSTION-VPC v2 loaded.
Raj Patel: FYI added a temporary manual node template with fewer init hooks to reduce provider calls. will create 2 nodes manually if API allows.
Diego Ramos: manual creation attempt: `terraform apply -target=module.acme_node[0]` -> provider returned 429 again. retrying with single node.
CustomerOps - Karen (ACME): customer infra confirmed they bumped rate limit for 2 clients; they opened a temporary allowance for our cluster. should be effective in ~90s.
Diego Ramos: nodes now transitioning to Ready. `kubectl get nodes | grep acme`: shows +2 Ready GPUs.
Priya Singh: metrics: error rate down to 12%, latency p95 ~2.1s. queue length halved. good sign.
Maya (sre-oncall): keep monitoring for 20m. we still need followups: 1) formal postmortem, 2) recommend provider-side rate limits and pre-warm guidance to customer, 3) add autoscaler detection for provider-429 and adaptive backoff.
Raj Patel: starting incident timeline notes. paging handoff: I'm good to stay until stable, but if it goes past 13:00 UTC I'll hand to night oncall Raj (jk) — real note: handoff to Raj in ~30m if stable. :slightly_smiling_face:
Diego Ramos: adding a short-term alert to monitoring: if queued_request_count > 200 after 20m -> re-open pager.
CustomerOps - Karen (ACME): customers reporting recovery, thanks team. will keep ticket open with our infra for permanent quota increase.
Maya (sre-oncall): 10m check-in: system stable, autoscaler no longer requesting >3 nodes concurrently, provider rate limit cleared, no new 502s for 6m. moving to mitigated state.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-4321 status changed to MITIGATED by Maya (sre-oncall).
Maya (sre-oncall): postmortem owners: Diego (cause triage), Priya (runtime mitigations), Raj (autoscaler improvements). I'll draft incident summary and include remediation actions: adapt backoff for 429, add dynamic provisionConcurrency, customer playbook for rate-limited providers.
Raj Patel: noted. handing off to follow-up thread. closing oncall here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
